findings.description: The database password is interpolated into EC2 user data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data and the resulting file can be accessed by processes or users that compromise the instance, exposing a long-lived database credential.

The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, which creates a public endpoint and weakens intended network segmentation. The current security-group ingress limits connections to the VPC CIDR, but the database remains unnecessarily internet-addressable.
storage_encrypted = false leaves RDS database storage, automated backups, and snapshots unencrypted at rest.

The EC2-assumable application role is granted s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* against every resource. Compromise of the attached application instance would yield broad control-plane and data access, including privilege-escalation-capable paths.

MySQL port 3306 is open to the entire VPC CIDR rather than being restricted to the application security group or specifically authorized clients. Any compromised or unauthorized workload in the VPC can attempt to reach the database.

The database security group allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This removes egress network segmentation and permits arbitrary outbound connections from the database host if it is compromised.
